_provenance_note: Created 2026-08-19 (sprint 002 ticket 001, clasi/sprints/002-zetuv-bench-square-tour-wheels-demo/) by copying data/tovez_nocal.json (the no-calibration template) verbatim and changing only identity/connection to name this file's robot and, after the bench pass below, the motors.left_port/right_port/fwd_sign_left/fwd_sign_right wiring facts. zetuv had NO prior configuration anywhere (not in this repo's data/, not in radio-robot-elite's data/robots/ -- confirmed by the sprint's own issue recon) and its hardware has never been bench-measured before today, so tovez_nocal.json (NOT the fully-calibrated tovez.json) is the honest starting point -- see sprint.md's own Design Rationale for why tovez.json's camera-fitted calibration values would be dishonest to carry onto unverified hardware. EVERY GROUP BELOW OTHER THAN identity/connection/motors.left_port/motors.right_port/motors.fwd_sign_left/motors.fwd_sign_right IS AN UNTOUCHED TEMPLATE DEFAULT, copied from a DIFFERENT physical robot (tovez), not measured on zetuv, and not appropriate for anything beyond an uncalibrated square-ish demo -- this includes geometry (trackwidth/rotation calibration), drive (duty_per_speed/wheel_gain), wheel_control (all inert/zero, matching the no-cal tier), planner/planner_shaper/navigator (tovez's own bench-measured operating points, assumed-not-verified to transfer), otos, estimator, wheels (wheel_diameter_mm/ticks_per_rev -- plausibly identical hardware across Nezha units but not independently confirmed on zetuv), encoders, gripper, peripherals, and _legacy_drive_limits. Per sprint.md's own Out of Scope: 'Calibration beyond wiring/sign verification ... zetuv.json stays a no-calibration profile this sprint, same tier as its tovez_nocal.json template' -- travel_calib_left/travel_calib_right are therefore deliberately NOT added to the motors group below either, even though config.REQUIRED_KEYS wants them: tovez_nocal.json itself ships without them (this is a pre-existing property of the no-cal template, not introduced here), so config.load_robot_config() fail-closes (ConfigError: missing travel_calib_left/right) on this file exactly as it already does on tovez_nocal.json -- boot.py's documented fail-closed contract (banner/READY/diffdrive import still available; motion refused until a real config loads). This is why the bench wiring verification below is done via direct REPL diffdrive.configure() calls that bypass boot.py/config.py entirely (docs/bench-acceptance-procedures.md A.4's own documented use of the manual path), not via a successful automatic boot-time configure.

connection._connection_note: device_announcement_name=zetuv and radio_channel=3 are the two BENCH-DIRECTED facts for this ticket (stakeholder/issue recon: `mbdeploy list` on 2026-08-19 confirmed zetuv at UID 9906360200052820312bde85515a72e6000000006e052820, /dev/cu.usbmodem2121202; radio_channel 3 matches this bench's existing convention, same as tovez.json's own channel -- not independently re-derived, just applied). serial_last_6=052820 is the last 6 hex characters of that same bench-confirmed UID (per this repo's own tovez.json precedent of deriving this field from 'the last-6 fragment of the device UID') -- used only for boot.py's banner suffix (_identity_lines()), NOT independently read back from an on-device serial announcement (none exists until this file is written to the device and rebooted). FLAGGED: this UID's trailing segment (000000006e052820) is shared verbatim by every board on this bench (getez, zavaz) -- it is a board-family/interface-chip suffix, not a per-board discriminator, so this value does not uniquely distinguish zetuv from its bench siblings within the banner text alone; recorded honestly rather than presented as a stronger identifier than it is. wifi_ip is the unmodified tovez_nocal.json template value -- WiFi is not used by this ticket (USB REPL only) and this address is not zetuv's own; left in place as an inert template default, not a claim about zetuv's network configuration.

geometry._rotation_calibration_note: 125-007 (adjacent-sim-plant-rotation-calibration-for-angle-stop-move-overshoot.md): sim-plant-measured, NOT camera-measured -- these correct the SIM plant's own ANGLE-stop coast-down overshoot (WheelPlant's first-order tau=0.13s duty->velocity lag, TestSim/wheel_plant.h -- the wheels keep coasting for a beat after the stop threshold fires, same physical mechanism real hardware's own actuation lag produces, .clasi/knowledge/actuation-latency-delay-in-plan.md), NOT geometry/stiction (contrast tovez.json's own hardware fit). Measured at omega=+/-2.0 rad/s (square_tour.py's own runTurnMove() rate) against SimLoop.get_true_pose(): identity calibration overshoots by a roughly-constant +11.8..+13.0 deg for target angles >=45 deg (45->56.9, 90->103.0, 180->193.0), least-squares-fit over that range to gain~1.006/offset~12.1 deg. Verified after fitting: 90 deg lands at 90.2 (err +0.2), 180 deg at 179.9 (err -0.1); the fit is intentionally NOT tuned for very small angles (<45 deg), which square_tour.py never commands (every corner is exactly 90 deg) and which the coast-down model saturates nonlinearly toward zero anyway (15 deg identity-overshoot measured +6.5, not +13 -- a single affine pair cannot cover both regimes, and this ticket's only consumer needs 90 deg). Requires 125-007's own sim_configure_drivetrain() plumbing (sim_ctypes.cpp/sim_boot_config.py) to take effect at all -- editing this JSON alone was previously a silent no-op for the sim path (SimHarness's own App::RobotLoop never got setRotationCalibration() called before that ticket). Symmetric pos/neg because the sim plant has no directional asymmetry coded (WheelPlant's dv/dt model is sign-symmetric); confirmed by measuring both directions. NOT a substitute for tovez.json's own camera-measured hardware values -- see that file's own note for why hardware needs a DIFFERENT (negative-offset) correction for a different physical reason. INHERITED UNCHANGED from tovez_nocal.json for zetuv (sprint 002 ticket 001) -- not re-derived, not bench-verified on zetuv.

motors._vel_gains_domain: duty [-1,1] (NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid); NOT the old PWM-percent scale
motors._neutral_note: NEUTRAL baseline (stakeholder 2026-07-18): this is the no-calibration profile, so the gains are the most vanilla usable set, not a tuning. vel_kp = 0.002 = 1/500: full duty at the plant's ~500 mm/s full-scale speed (duty = error / v_max, the plainest proportional normalization; a pure-P loop droops by design). vel_kff = 0.002 = 1/500 too -- the SAME vanilla inverse-plant slope, and the open-loop law itself: with the PID disabled (TestGUI PID checkbox) the motor drives duty = kff * velocityTarget, so kff=0 would make PID-off dead rather than open-loop. vel_ki = 0 (no integrator), vel_imax/vel_kaw = 0 (inert with ki=0; kaw=0 = anti-windup off). vel_filt = 1.0 (no EMA smoothing, raw measured velocity; NOTE: no live SET key -- build-time bake only). This config is the source of truth for the drive/control parameters -- there are to be NO tunable defaults in the source. (The former UPDATE 2026-07-20 sentence here, about a half-dozen sibling control.* heading/distance/model-tau keys, is moot -- those keys were deleted, 119-003 config-attic sweep, no living consumer survived 115-003's motion-stack excision.)
motors._port_note: BENCH-MEASURED 2026-08-19 (sprint 002 ticket 001, zetuv, direct USB /dev/cu.usbmodem2121202, mpremote-run REPL scripts, smallest-visible-pulse protocol per docs/bench-acceptance-procedures.md A.4 -- full observation log in docs/bench-log-zetuv-2026-08-19.md). Method: diffdrive.configure(left_port=2, right_port=1, fwd_sign_left=1, fwd_sign_right=1, ...) then EACH port driven ALONE (never both at once for this determination) via driveDuty(), reading diffdrive.output()'s positionLeft/positionRight before/during/after each pulse -- encoder deltas are the ground truth, per this ticket's own instruction, not a visual judgment (this agent has no camera/vision access to the physical bench). RESULT: port 2 alone (0.20 duty, 400ms lease) moved positionLeft 0->2->5 (positive, higher breakaway than port 1 -- 0.06 duty was not enough to move it, 0.20 was); port 1 alone (0.06 duty, 300ms lease) moved positionRight 0->11->61 (positive, moves easily even at low duty). Both ports independently confirmed connected (I2C ack) AND encoder-responsive. Since a POSITIVE commanded duty produced a POSITIVE position delta on EACH port individually at fwd_sign=+1 (identity, no correction), fwd_sign_left=1/fwd_sign_right=1 (unchanged from the template's fwd_sign_left, but fwd_sign_right flipped from the template's -1 to +1) is the value that keeps each port's own 'positive duty -> positive/forward encoder response' consistent -- NOT copied from tovez.json/gopiv.json's own (different, opposite-pair) wiring fixes, independently derived from zetuv's own pulses. CAVEAT, flagged rather than hidden: this determination rests on INDIVIDUAL single-port pulses, deliberately never both ports driven together for the port/sign determination itself (ticket's own 'one wheel at a time when probing' discipline) -- a SEPARATE COMBINED-drive anomaly was found and is NOT resolved by this note; see this file's own _combined_drive_anomaly_note below and the bench log for the full writeup. What was NOT independently verified this session: true visual 'which physical side is left' (no camera/vision tool available to this agent) -- left_port=2/right_port=1's LABEL assignment (as opposed to the wiring/sign facts above, which are measured) follows this fleet's own established convention (tovez.json/gopiv.json both also use left_port=2/right_port=1), flagged as convention-matched rather than independently re-derived.
motors._combined_drive_anomaly_note: ROOT-CAUSED AND RESOLVED, sprint 002 ticket 002, 2026-08-19 (full write-up: docs/bench-log-zetuv-2026-08-19.md). Ticket 001's original finding (BOTH ports driven simultaneously left port 2/left stationary while port 1/right moved briskly) was NEVER actually about combined-vs-single-wheel driving -- ticket 002 reproduced 'left stuck' with LEFT DRIVEN ALONE too, under the SAME diffdrive.configure(..., max_duty=0.15) convention ticket 001 used, ruling out I2C interference/collision between channels as the cause. Root cause: max_duty and driveDuty()'s dutyLeft/dutyRight are PERCENT (0-100) in the vendored kernel (vendor/differential_drive.h's own Config.maxDuty/Command.dutyLeft field comments, '// [%]'), NOT the [-1,1] fraction native/moddiffdrive.cpp's and native/README.md's own (now-corrected) documentation claimed. max_duty=0.15 was therefore an authority rail of ~0.15%, far below the write path's own 3% output-deadband floor (NezhaMotor::writeShapedDuty()) -- every nonzero commanded duty silently boosted to that SAME ~3% floor regardless of what was requested, a value sitting right at port 2/left's own breakaway threshold: sometimes just enough (ticket 001's single-wheel test, 5 ticks of motion), usually not (ticket 001's two combined trials AND ticket 002's own reproduction, alone or combined, 0 ticks every time). Fix: use the kernel's real percent convention (bench-verified sprint 002 ticket 002: max_duty=25.0 rail, driveDuty(20.0, 20.0, ...) or lower -- 6.0 duty already moves both wheels reliably, alone and combined, repeated across multiple independent trials including the full 8-segment square-tour demo, src/demo_square.py). No I2C broker/binding change was needed or made -- this was a call-site units bug, not a hardware, vendor, or native/ code fault. The safety-critical property (duty zeroes at lease expiry, no drift after) held correctly in every trial throughout both tickets, unaffected by this units bug -- see this file's own top-level _provenance_note and both bench log sections.

drive._drive_calibration_note: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
drive._wheel_correction_note: IDENTITY as of 2026-07-31 (stakeholder). The fitted values (tovez: gain ~1.47) were measured against a duty_per_speed that was itself wrong by ~1.6x, so the pair was circularly calibrated -- each fitted against the other's error -- and the correction ended up pointing the WRONG WAY: it divided a 150mm/s request down to 96 before the duty conversion, on a robot that was already under-delivering. duty_per_speed is now a baked measured constant (App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed), so this affine stage has nothing left to correct and is held at identity. Do not re-fit it against duty_per_speed again; refit only against camera-measured travel, and say so here. gain 1 / intercept 0 = no correction.

wheels._wheels_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (sprint 004 ticket 001, clasi/sprints/004-square-tour-travel-units-fix/ -- root cause of the 'legs run ~4-5x short' bug, docs/bench-log-zetuv-2026-08-19.md). The prior values (wheel_diameter_mm=80.77, ticks_per_rev=360, ticks_per_mm=1.4187) were UNVERIFIED tovez_nocal.json template defaults, never independently measured on any real Nezha unit in this repo's data/ -- including tovez.json itself, whose own wheels block carries the identical unqualified trio with no camera/bench provenance note, unlike every other calibrated group in that file. The arithmetic (ticks_per_mm = ticks_per_rev / (pi * wheel_diameter_mm)) was correct; the two inputs were simply wrong, producing an encoder-termination target ~4.2-5.3x too small -- matching the stakeholder's live observation (2026-08-19) that a '500 mm' leg turned the wheels only ~270 deg (0.75 rev) instead of the ~3.3-3.6 rev 500 mm actually needs. FIX: derived from the stakeholder's own empirical bench anchor per the issue's explicit 'empirical wins on conflict' instruction -- sprint-002 run-1's four leg segments averaged 731.4 counts of encoder delta for that same observed 0.75 rev (docs/bench-log-zetuv-2026-08-19.md Sec 15), giving an empirical counts-per-revolution of 731.4/0.75=975.2 (the issue's own stated range is ~870-1080; its midpoint, 975, is used here). Combined with the issue's stated wheel circumference (~145 mm) this gives wheel_diameter_mm=145.0/pi=46.1521 (a far more physically plausible size for this classroom kit's wheel than the old 80.77), ticks_per_rev=975.0 (held as a float -- a derived bench figure, not a manufacturer tick-count spec), ticks_per_mm=975.0/145.0=6.7241. CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST, AND FOUND TO CONFLICT WITH, tovez.json's own motors.travel_calib_left/right (0.7837 mm/deg of raw encoder shaft rotation, per vendor/nezha_motor.h's own comments, at 10 counts/degree since the raw register reports tenths of a degree): that implies ticks_per_mm~=12.76, ~1.9x this value. Per the issue's own instruction the empirical anchor governs, not travel_calib -- also note travel_calib feeds a DIFFERENT kernel field (fullDutyVelocity, VELOCITY-mode drive()'s plant-gain calibration) that src/demo_square.py never reads (it drives via driveDuty() directly, bypassing config.py/travel_calib entirely), so travel_calib was never the field actually causing this bug regardless of the conflict. Still NOT independently camera/tape-verified on zetuv's own physical wheel -- an empirical bench-derived correction, not a fresh measured pass; worth superseding with a real camera/tape calibration pass. This group remains outside data/robot_config.schema.json's modeled groups (schema 'known gap', same as before this fix) -- this note does not change that.

_legacy_drive_limits._units_note: All speeds mm/s; motor_deadband is mm/s (stakeholder 2026-07-20): the smallest wheel speed that actually moves the plant, = outputDeadband(0.03 duty) / vel_kff(0.002) = 15 mm/s. Firmware/host convert to duty as needed; no code default -- config is the source of truth.
